newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel repeats convergence comes before timetable.
newsitem.headline: Waigel repeats convergence comes before timetable.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Monday reiterated that adherence to the Maastricht Treaty's convergence criteria took precedence over the timetable for monetary union.
"Convergence determines the timetable," Waigel told reporters in Brussels where he was attending a meeting of European Union finance ministers.
He declined to answer questions about a possible postponement of monetary union. "I will not take part in this discussion."

"Everybody is making efforts to fulfil the criteria," Waigel said, adding that the decision on which countries qualify to form monetary union at the scheduled January 1, 1999 launch date will not be taken until 1998.
"That is the time for the decision in Europe and not before and not afterwards," Waigel said.
Earlier, Waigel was quoted in Bild newspaper on Monday as saying: "There won't be any soft euro with me. The important thing is: criteria have precedence over timetable."
"We shall in the next nine months do all we can to fulfil the Maastricht stability criteria."
The comments fuelled speculation about a possible delay amid growing doubts that Germany will be able to qualify for monetary union on time.
